title: Nth Fibonacci in O(log n)
statement:
The Fibonacci numbers are defined by `F(0) = 0`, `F(1) = 1` and `F(k) = F(k - 1) + F(k - 2)` for `k ≥ 2`.

Given `n`, compute `F(n)` **modulo** `1000000007`. The value of `n` can be as large as `10^18`, so you cannot step through the sequence one term at a time: you need a method whose running time is logarithmic in `n`.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer asked for a logarithmic-time approach to the nth Fibonacci number. Know at least two ways to get there, for example matrix exponentiation and fast doubling, and be able to compare them.

examples.explanation: F(100) = 354224848179261915075, which leaves remainder 687995182 when divided by 1000000007.

hints: Counting up one term at a time takes O(n), which is hopeless for n = 10^18.
The pair (F(k), F(k+1)) can be advanced by one step with a fixed 2x2 matrix [[1,1],[1,0]]. Raising that matrix to the nth power by repeated squaring takes O(log n) multiplications.

Alternatively use the doubling identities F(2k) = F(k)·(2·F(k+1) − F(k)) and F(2k+1) = F(k)² + F(k+1)². Keep every product reduced modulo 1000000007; in languages with 64-bit integers, products of two reduced values still fit.
